title: cukereuse-subscenarios: paraphrase-robust subsequence mining and three-scope refactoring-candidate ranking for Cucumber/Gherkin
description:
Reproduction package for Mining Subscenario Refactoring Opportunities in Behaviour-Driven Software Test Suites: ML Classifiers and LLM-Judge Baselines (Mughal, Fatima, Bilal, 2026; arXiv:2605.14568; under peer review at Software Quality Journal).

The deposit ships the full paper-3 pipeline and its derived analytical artefacts: a slice inventory of every contiguous L-step window (L = 2..18) across 126,621 named scenarios in 339 repositories / 276 distinct upstream owners; exact-pattern recurrence counts under three scopes (within-file, within-repo, cross-organisational); a 200-slice author-labelled pool with a 60-slice overlap subset (Fleiss' κ = 0.560 / 0.788 on extraction-worthy / mechanism labels); XGBoost extraction-worthy and mechanism classifiers (5-fold OOF F1 = 0.891 / accuracy = 0.965); a rule-baseline comparison via McNemar's test; and an LLM-judge replication on the same 200-slice pool using two open-weight models via OpenRouter (openai/gpt-oss-120b, inclusionai/ling-2.6-1t).

Contents: analysis/ (~153 MB derived artefacts — slices, cluster ids, exact-subsequence ranking, classifier predictions, per-fold metrics, corpus and population rollups, HTML candidate report), methodology/ (rubric, per-author labels, labelling pool, LLM-judge raw outputs and agreement metrics), scripts/ (21 numbered pipeline scripts), DATA_CARD.md (per-artefact provenance and schema), CITATION.cff, LICENSE (Apache-2.0), NOTICE, pyproject.toml, README.md.

Not redistributed (regenerable from slices.parquet via scripts/04_slice_embedding_clustering.py): slice_embeddings.npz (820 MB) and cluster_embeddings.npz (89 MB). The shipped slice_clusters.parquet already carries the cluster ids those embeddings produced.

This is paper 3 of a three-paper arc on test reuse in Cucumber-style BDD. Paper 1 (Mughal 2024) introduced three concrete reuse mechanisms in Cucumber-Java; paper 2 (cukereuse, github.com/amughalbscs16/cukereuse-release) measured step-level duplication on a 1.1M-step open corpus; paper 3 lifts the analysis from steps to contiguous step subsequences (slices), ranks them by refactoring suitability, and maps each surviving candidate to one of paper 1's three mechanisms.
